content.title: Colorado Front Range Trail in Arvada
content.summary: The City of Arvada, in partnership with Jefferson County Open Space, is moving forward with the construction of a 1.7-mile segment of the Colorado Front Range Trail (CFRT), which will connect the Ralston Creek Trail to 82nd Ave. A matching grant of $2.4 million from the Jefferson County Trails Partnership Program will cover half of the project's costs, with the remainder funded by the city. The project is currently in the design phase, with construction expected to begin in spring 2026 and the trail segment anticipated to open in fall 2026.
content.body:
The City of Arvada and Jefferson County Open Space are partnering on the design and build of the next critical piece of the Colorado Front Range Trail (CFRT). The missing trail segment is 1.7 miles long and is located north of the Arvada-Blunn Reservoir and south of 82nd Ave.

The [Jefferson County-led feasibility study](https://www.jeffco.us/DocumentCenter/View/33386/Colorado-Front-Range-Trail-Feasibility-Study) completed in April 2023 supports this next phase of work.

On Jan. 30th, 2024, the Jefferson County Board of Commissioners awarded the City of Arvada a matching grant of $2.4 million through the Jefferson County Trails Partnership Program to construct the missing segment of the CFRT in Arvada. The grant award represents 50% of the total project cost with the other 50% allocated by the City.

The City of Arvada's Parks and Urban Design team has hired CEI-Muller to design and construct the trail. As of July 2025, the project is in construction documentation.

The City reviewed and analyzed three trail alignment options and chose a preferred alignment that scored the highest based on safety, maintenance and user experience.

All three alignment options connect from the Ralston Creek Trail north of Arvada-Blunn Reservoir and go north toward 82nd Ave.

- The preferred alignment, shown in purple on the map below, runs north-south and then turns and heads west toward Highway 93, stopping at an overlook at the top of the grade and holding the trail back a ways from the highway. A spur trail that could connect to the Pattridge Open Space Trailhead is also recommended, but not along the formal CFRT. The spur trail is also not currently funded.
- The west alignment, shown in blue on the map below, takes users northwest to Highway 93.
- The east alignment, shown in green on the map below, takes users directly north to 82nd Ave.
- The Pattridge Open Space connection, shown in red on the map below, takes users to the trailhead at Pattridge Open Space.

![CFRT Alternates](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6107)

## Background on the Colorado Front Range Trail

Initiated by Colorado Parks and Wildlife in 2003, the vision of the CFRT is to create a multi-purpose trail from Wyoming to New Mexico along the Front Range of Colorado.

Once completed, the CFRT would include more than 875 miles of trail along the Front Range connected to the natural and cultural features of the Colorado landscape. The CFRT uses existing trails as much as possible, and approximately one third of the trail corridor (270 miles) is finished.

## General Project Timeline

- April 2023: [CFRT Feasibility Study - North Table Mountain Park to Boulder County](https://www.jeffco.us/DocumentCenter/View/33386/Colorado-Front-Range-Trail-Feasibility-Study) - Completed
- January 2024: City of Arvada awarded matching grant from the Jefferson County Trails Partnership Program
- Early Summer 2024: City of Arvada Parks and Urban Design puts design-build contract out to bid
- Summer 2024: City of Arvada Parks and Urban Design team selects contractor
- Fall 2024: Design of the trail segment begins
- Fall 2025: Permitting of the trail segment begins
- Spring 2026: Construction of the trail segments begins
- Fall 2026: Trail segment opens

### How the trail segment aligns with other master planning efforts

Locally, completion of the CFRT supports goals outlined in [Arvada's 2016 Parks, Trails, and Open Space Master Plan](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=68c0b26db9532). The new segment of trail will meet a growing demand for increased access to open spaces and trails, creating connections closer to home, and improving connectivity within and across Arvada as well as the larger regional trail system as a whole.

Building this segment of the CFRT also aligns with guidance outlined in the following plans and initiatives:

- [Jeffco Trails Plan](https://www.jeffco.us/DocumentCenter/View/23641/Jeffco-Trails-Plan-Adopted)
- [Jeffco Bike Plan](https://www.jeffco.us/DocumentCenter/View/32001/Jefferson-County-Bicycle-Plan-2022-PDF)
- [Jeffco Open Space's Conservation Greenprint 5-Year Plan](https://www.jeffco.us/DocumentCenter/View/22753/Jeffco-Open-Space-Conservation-Greenprint)
- [CDOT’s WestConnect Coalition’s Planning and Environmental Linkages Study](https://www.codot.gov/projects/studies/study-archives/westconnect-coalition-pel-study)
